what: The score combines exact insertion distance with capacity-aware lookahead. It mildly penalizes residual capacity and scans the remaining customers for a nearby feasible successor, preferring successors that would also leave little unused capacity. If no successor fits, unused capacity receives a stronger route-closing penalty. Each evaluation costs O(length of current route + number of unassigned customers) time and O(1) extra space.
why: Insertion delta preserves geometric quality, while the continuation term encourages spatial chains that are likely to remain useful after intra-route 2-opt. The adaptive packing terms address both ordinary capacity pressure and highly uneven demands, including customers consuming most of a vehicle. Scaling by mean depot radius makes the demand penalties commensurate with distance across coordinate scales. This is still a local heuristic: its one-customer lookahead cannot detect multi-customer packing combinations, and strong geometric or demand pathologies may require different coefficient tradeoffs. No empirical performance claim is implied.
